clue.text: Stand up to model after work

indicators.note: the model comes after the work in the answer, so this places the two pieces in order

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a musical work
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone resists a fashion model who turns up once the working day is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose someone is to resist or confront them, the same as standing up to them.

clue.text: Type of shoe in box, for display

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words box, for display

explanation.surface: A pair of shoes sits in a shop's display box.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a classic lace-up shoe with closed lacing, named after the university.

clue.text: Supreme soldier sitting on horse

indicators.note: in a down answer the soldier sits on top of the horse piece

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a mount is a horse one rides

explanation.surface: A top soldier rides a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means of chief importance, highest in rank: supreme.

clue.text: Sales pitch involving a new breed of 25

indicators.note: the sales pitch takes in the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a spiel is a glib, persuasive sales pitch

explanation.surface: A sales pitch features a new breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25 across, GUNDOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaniel is a family of gundog breeds used to flush and retrieve game.

clue.text: Dirk's case maybe found in second taxi taken by poet

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
a bard is a poet, Shakespeare being the Bard

explanation.surface: A dagger's sheath is discovered in a second taxi hired by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A dirk is a Scottish dagger; 'maybe' signals that its case is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath for a blade, and a dirk is one blade that would be kept in one.

clue.text: Heart set on article — an epergne, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down answer the heart piece is placed on top of the article piece

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
a piece is an article, as in a newspaper piece

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a particular item, an ornate table ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: An epergne is an ornamental stand of dishes for the middle of a dining table; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrepiece is a decoration placed in the middle of a table, of which an epergne is one kind.

clue.text: Pub: get value for money?

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to gain something is to get it

explanation.surface: A question whether a pub offers good value.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something bought cheaply, good value for the money spent.

clue.text: Irritate any number inside

indicators.note: the number piece goes within the word any

explanation.surface: Any number of people indoors can get on one's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate or vex them.

clue.text: Costume to get on for equestrian event

parts.note: a dress is a costume or outfit
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: A rider puts on an outfit before a horse show.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is a competitive discipline in which a horse performs precise movements, an equestrian event.

clue.text: The old lady, impressed by military building's layout

indicators.note: pressed into the fort, so the mother's letters go inside the building's

parts.note: a fort is a military building
'old lady' is slang for one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: Someone's mother admires the floor plan of an army fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed by' looks like it means admiring, but here it means physically pressed into.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the arrangement or design of something, which is its layout.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: to ... (stress on the second syllable) is to enchant or charm
an ... (stress on the first syllable) is a door or way in

explanation.surface: Someone talks their way into a place by sheer charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling gives a verb meaning to enchant and a noun meaning a doorway, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Jogger grabbing a rest

indicators.note: the reminder takes hold of the a, so it goes inside

parts.note: something that jogs the memory is a reminder

explanation.surface: A runner seizes a moment to catch their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner, but it means something that jogs the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, as in 'the rest of the money'.

clue.text: Dogmatic, a director in cast

indicators.note: letters cast about are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A director inflexibly picks the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as the actors, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person applies theory rigidly whatever the circumstances, which is being dogmatic.

clue.text: Fool sheltering next to deep chasm

indicators.note: the fool shelters the other word inside itself

parts.note: an ass is a fool
by means beside or next to, as in 'sit by me'

explanation.surface: An idiot takes cover beside a deep gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless pit or gulf, a very deep chasm.

clue.text: Senate at first undecided on widespread government expenditure

indicators.note: the senate and undecided pieces sit on, after, the widespread piece

parts.note: something widespread is public, generally known or shared

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Senate is all that is taken

parts.note: a matter still undecided is pending

explanation.surface: A senate dithers over a sweeping plan for state expenditure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the senate and undecided pieces come after the widespread one, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Public spending is the money a state lays out on services, which is government expenditure.

clue.text: Very confused at home, a Greek character, theologian, over the Parisian

indicators.note: in a down answer the earlier pieces sit over the last one

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Greek scholar and a theologian are at home together, baffled by French.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a muddle is thoroughly confused or disorganised.

clue.text: Italian lady heading off –- extremely nescient, lacking in education

indicators.note: the first letter of the lady's title is removed

parts.note: signora is the Italian for a married woman, a lady

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of nescient are used

explanation.surface: An Italian woman leaves, deeply ignorant and poorly schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips S from SIGNORA, leaving IGNORA. Nescient is a rare word for ignorant, so the surface is a little self-referential.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant person lacks knowledge, often through a lack of schooling.

clue.text: Lose control, as protesters sometimes do?

definitions.meaning: to become overexcited and lose self-control
demonstrators staging a sit-in may literally be picked up and removed by police

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper is compared with what happens to demonstrators at a sit-in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being so excited one stops behaving sensibly; the literal sense is being physically removed.

clue.text: A married girl in the USA

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married in genealogies and forms
Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wedded young woman lives in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: America is the everyday name for the United States of America.

clue.text: Attack a sailor on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the words are to be said aloud

parts.note: a salt, or old salt, is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is assaulted while broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack, and to assault is to attack.

clue.text: Put on leg pad at the end

parts.note: a leg of a journey is a stage

indicators.note: only the final letter of pad is taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer straps on a leg pad at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cricket pad; 'leg' is a stage of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on.

clue.text: Small amount of uranium to be imported by when?

indicators.note: the uranium is brought into the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: once can mean when, as in 'once you arrive, call me'
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A query about when a little uranium will be shipped into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, and figuratively any tiny quantity, as in 'an ounce of sense'.

clue.text: Pleasant entertaining English relative

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the English letter goes inside

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A pleasant English relative is good company.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relative.

clue.text: Mend set, in pieces, broken by American –- I can't afford not to

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are split open by the American piece going inside
a set lying in pieces is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: Someone must repair a broken set an American smashed, as they cannot pay for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' turns MEND SET into NEEDSMT; 'broken by' puts US inside, before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: From 'needs must when the devil drives': necessity compels, so one has no real choice but to do it.

clue.text: Bubbly at pier, provided as a drink to whet one's appetite

definitions.text: a drink to whet one's appetite

indicators.note: bubbling letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it's dry'

explanation.surface: Champagne is served at the pier as a pre-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne, the noun; it is the anagram signal on AT PIER, giving APERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Good open ground, initially, for retriever

parts.note: to undo a parcel is to open it

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word ground is used

explanation.surface: Fine open land is where a retriever first gets its exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog is bred to work with hunters, and a retriever is one such dog, fetching shot game.

clue.text: Adolescent brewed green tea

indicators.note: tea that is brewed is stewed and stirred, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A youngster has made a pot of green tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen, an adolescent.

clue.text: Go to a nurse about temperature

indicators.note: the a and nurse pieces go round the temperature piece

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A patient visits a nurse because of a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend a meeting or school is to go to it.
